packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response; packets 02 and 14 completed by further fresh readers after a display cap hid images, packet 17 reread by a fresh reader
text:
PACKET-08 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: No proposed identification of the work or author was in my context. Visible on the support itself are modern pencil labels "Stams, STA, Fag. 224-1r", "Stams, STA, Fag. 224-2r" (face 1) and "...224-1v", "...224-2v" (face 2), and on face 1 a small paper label straddling the bottom seam reading "Annales Silesiae / X/A14" (image-006/007 bottom). That label looks like a host-volume or shelf label, not an identification of this text, but I report it because it is a name-like title visible in the images. I did not use it. I did nothing beyond the reader brief: I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..014 in this packet, listed the packet directory to get filenames (did not open packet.json), and made two contrast-enhanced, enlarged crops of image-009 in my scratchpad to read the faint face-2 column.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- image-001 (face 1 overview) and image-008 (face 2 overview): a long vertical parchment strip, upright, about 13 cm wide x 36 cm high on the scale. It is two narrow strips joined along a vertical cut (dark line), labelled 224-1 (left on face 1) and 224-2 (right on face 1); on face 2 the order is reversed.
- The text runs continuously across the cut: words split by it continue on the other strip (e.g. "ibide|m", "si sitie|rit"). So the two strips are adjacent pieces of the same leaf.
- Face 1: one full-width column (col. A, about 30 written lines visible, upper ~1/4 of strip blank as top margin, lower ~1/3 blank as bottom margin), plus the left edge of a second column (col. B) at the far right, cut off by the strip edge. Two-column layout is therefore likely (tentative).
- Face 2: line ends of one column at the far left (cut), and one fuller column to its right (faint, water-stained, abraded right half). Column order on face 2 relative to face 1 is not certain.
- Script: small gothic book hand, brown ink, heavily abbreviated. Alternating red and blue initials (red I/C flourished in red; blue initials on face 1 col. A at "Benefacite" and at "Item idem", and at face 2 col. at "Item si"). Some words are underlined in ink, apparently marking quoted lemmata (e.g. "Diligite inimicos vestros", "Benefacite", "misericordiam volo et non sacrificium"). Red underlining once with a red flourish line (face 1 col. A line 11).
- Tentative interpretation: main-text quotations (underlined) followed by explanatory prose with chains of biblical citations ("Item ... ibidem", "Prov. xxv. ca.", "Luc. viii. ca.", "i. Re."), i.e. a commentary or treatise style. Not identified.

SELECTED SPANS: face 1 col. A in full (read across the cut by combining left-strip and right-strip tiles); face 1 col. B line beginnings (sample); face 2 main column (first ~20 lines) and the line ends at left (sample).
Overlaps: image-002/003 are the top halves of left/right strips (same lines); image-004/005 the middles; image-006/007 the bottoms. Lines overlap by several lines between 002-004 and 004-006 (e.g. "magnu(m)..." is 002 L16 and 004 L1). I number each combined line by both tiles and do not double count overlaps.

UNREAD / LIMITATIONS
- Face 1 col. A top lines 1-7 are pale; readings there are weak. Col. A lines 16-21 (left strip) are partly rubbed.
- Face 1 col. B and face 2 left column survive only as a few letters at each line, cut by the strip edges.
- Face 2 is heavily water-stained with pale abraded patches; the right half of the main column (image-010, image-012) is largely illegible to me even with contrast enhancement. Multispectral/UV imaging would likely help.
- The vertical cut between the two strips may have lost a narrow band of letters; where words seem to join across it I have marked "|", but a letter or two may be missing there.
- Clearest anchor phrases for a later source match: "Diligite inimicos vestros", "Benefacite", "Si videris asinum odientis te iacere sub onere non pertransibis sed sublevabis cum eo", "Prov. xxv ca. Si esurierit inimicus tuus ciba illum, si sitierit da ei aquam bibere", "Cum autem descendisset ... de monte secute sunt eum turbe multe, et ecce leprosus veniens adorabat eum dicens Domine si vis potes me mundare", "misericordiam volo et non sacrificium", "vade ad tuos et narra quanta fecit tibi deus", "qui me confessus fuerit coram hominibus confitebor et ego eum coram patre meo"; on face 2 "bethsabee", "Item si excusauit".
